title: One Canon: Collisions, Convergence, and Stale Asks

intelligence.essence: A shared system constantly manufactures duplicates — of IDs, of files, of documents, of work — and this block records the discipline of keeping exactly one canon without destroying history. Duplicate Smart Note IDs are repaired by renumbering the registry, never by deleting history, and a *skipped* repair is itself a recorded decision (SN-834). Two documents each claiming to be "the single canonical" one is a duplicate mechanism, caught by re-reading the sources before authoring a convergence (SN-898) — and semantic convergence never licenses calling two artifacts "the same" without a byte or provenance check (SN-930). Work that collides mid-flight is finished and transferred, never restarted or duplicated (SN-933); work already done is delta-checked, never re-executed (SN-941); and "canonical" itself is a reconciliation result — main's ledger was wrong about its own decision log until an orphan branch's verified record was cherry-picked forward (SN-864).
intelligence.human_view: A busy team is a machine for making two of everything: two notes with one number, two documents both calling themselves *the* standard, two people fixing the same thing, two requests for work already done. Keeping one canon isn't tidiness — it's what makes the record readable by the next person. These notes share a temperament: slow down at the moment of duplication, check what's actually true (bytes, provenance, the board), and resolve the collision in the open — renumbering instead of deleting, folding instead of competing, transferring instead of restarting, and answering a stale request with what changed instead of doing the work twice.
intelligence.child_view: Imagine the class makes two birthday posters for the same party, and both say "THE poster." You don't throw one away or hang both and confuse everyone. You check: are they really the same poster? (Hold them side by side.) If a friend already finished the poster, you don't make a third — you look at theirs and add only what's missing. And if two toys have the same name tag, you change one tag — you never throw a toy away just to fix the tags.
intelligence.grandma_view: It's the family Bible problem, dear: three copies, two with the same pages numbered differently, one with grandmother's notes in the margins. You don't burn any of them. You check which is the true record — sometimes it's the copy in the attic, not the one on the shelf — you renumber carefully, you write down what you did and why, and you never, ever pretend two different books are the same book just because their covers match.
intelligence.ai_view: On any duplicate ID: renumber, never delete; clear new numbers across main + open PRs; record skipped repairs as decisions (SN-834). Count integration from substance, not citations; flag duplicates instead of normalizing them (SN-830). Fold filenames to lowercase in the tree check, base included (SN-831). Treat "canonical" as a verdict to earn by recompute; cherry-pick verified orphan work forward (SN-864). Before drafting any convergence, re-read the sources at their current tips; delta-fold or stand down (SN-898). Before any sameness claim, run byte-identity → provenance → structural comparison, in that order (SN-930). On a mid-flight collision: finish, transfer to the assigned owner for verification, forbid parallel builds, post the resolution on the board (SN-933). On any incoming ask: run the completion check before executing; deliver deltas, not duplicates (SN-941).
intelligence.what_it_means: The eight notes are one conservation law: **the system's memory must contain each thing once, under one name, with its history intact.** Every mechanism here protects a different face of that law — registry (SN-834), counting (SN-830), filenames (SN-831), truth-location (SN-864), documents (SN-898, SN-930), in-flight work (SN-933), and the work queue itself (SN-941). The failures they prevent are also one failure: a second copy quietly becoming a second truth, after which no one can say which record the next decision should trust.
whats_inside: Dedup = renumber the registry, delete nothing; canonical keeps its ID by first-claim; new numbers clear main + all open PRs; a skipped repair is a recorded decision with doctrine (SN-834).
Citations are not integration; honest zeros beat inflated positives; duplicate and vanity IDs are flagged, never normalized (SN-830).
Case-only filename differences are collisions on case-insensitive filesystems; check is lowercase-folded `ls-tree` incl. base; gate belongs in CI (SN-831).
Canonical = verified reconciliation, wherever it lives; cherry-pick verified commits forward, never redo (SN-864).
Re-read sources on current bytes before authoring any convergence; a converged source gets a delta-fold, not a competitor (SN-898).
Sameness requires byte-identity (or a verified provenance chain); convergence licenses "converges with" + a list of distinct contributions (SN-930).
Mid-flight collisions resolve finish → transfer → no parallel build → board-posted resolution; the dispatcher owns the miss (SN-933).
Incoming asks are claims of pending work; verify (memory → board → bytes) and post deltas only when complete (SN-941).
